# dtrevc3

> Computes some or all of the right and/or left eigenvectors of a real upper quasi-triangular matrix T.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dtrevc3 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dtrevc3';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dtrevc3(
    order,
    side, howmny,
    SELECT, strideSELECT,
    N,
    T, LDT,
    VL, LDVL,
    VR, LDVR,
    mm,
    M,
    WORK
) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `side` | `"left" \| "right" \| "both"` | `'right'`: compute right eigenvectors only; `'left'`: compute left eigenvectors only; `'both'`: compute both right and left eigenvectors. |
| `howmny` | `"all" \| "backtransform" \| "selected"` | `'all'`: compute all right and/or left eigenvectors; `'backtransform'`: compute all right and/or left eigenvectors, backtransformed by the matrices in VR and/or VL; `'selected'`: compute selected right and/or left eigenvectors, as indicated by the logical array SELECT. |
| `SELECT` | `Uint8Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · If `howmny === 'selected'`, SELECT specifies the eigenvectors to be computed. |
| ↳ `strideSELECT` | `integer` | Stride length for `SELECT` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | The order of the matrix T.<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `T` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | The upper quasi-triangular matrix T in Schur canonical form. |
| ↳ `LDT` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `T`<br>Requires `LDT ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `VL` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × mm</sub> | **in/out** · On entry, if `side === 'left'` or `side === 'both'` and `howmny === 'backtransform'`, VL must contain an N-by-N matrix Q (usually the orthogonal matrix Q of Schur vectors returned by DHSEQR). On exit, if `side === 'left'` or `side === 'both'`, VL contains: if `howmny === 'all'`, the matrix Y of left eigenvectors of T; if `howmny === 'backtransform'`, the matrix Q\*Y; if `howmny === 'selected'`, the left eigenvectors of T specified by SELECT, stored consecutively in the columns of VL, in the same order as their eigenvalues. |
| ↳ `LDVL` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `VL`<br>Rejects `ldvl < 1 \|\| ((side === 'left' \|\| side === 'both') && ldvl < N)` |
| `VR` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × mm</sub> | **in/out** · On entry, if `side === 'right'` or `side === 'both'` and `howmny === 'backtransform'`, VR must contain an N-by-N matrix Q (usually the orthogonal matrix Q of Schur vectors returned by DHSEQR). On exit, if `side === 'right'` or `side === 'both'`, VR contains: if `howmny === 'all'`, the matrix X of right eigenvectors of T; if `howmny === 'backtransform'`, the matrix Q\*X; if `howmny === 'selected'`, the right eigenvectors of T specified by SELECT, stored consecutively in the columns of VR, in the same order as their eigenvalues. |
| ↳ `LDVR` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `VR`<br>Rejects `ldvr < 1 \|\| ((side === 'right' \|\| side === 'both') && ldvr < N)` |
| `mm` | `NonNegativeInteger` | The number of columns in the arrays VL and/or VR. |
| `M` | `Int32Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the number of columns in the arrays VL and/or VR actually used to store the eigenvectors |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ max(1, 3 * N)</sub> | **out** · Caller-provided workspace of at least `max( 1, 3 * N )` elements; when back-transforming, at least `N + 2*N*8` enables the blocked back-transformation; `null` allocates the optimal size `max( 1, N + 2*N*NB )`, with NB from `ilaenv` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `side`:

  -   `= 'R'`: compute right eigenvectors only;
  -   `= 'L'`: compute left eigenvectors only;
  -   `= 'B'`: compute both right and left eigenvectors.
- `howmny`:

  -   `= 'A'`: compute all right and/or left eigenvectors;
  -   `= 'B'`: compute all right and/or left eigenvectors, backtransformed by the matrices in `VR` and/or `VL`;
  -   `= 'S'`: compute selected right and/or left eigenvectors, as indicated by the logical array `SELECT`.
- `SELECT`: If `HOWMNY = 'S'`, `SELECT` specifies the eigenvectors to be computed. If w(j) is a real eigenvalue, the corresponding real eigenvector is computed if `SELECT(j)` is .TRUE.. If w(j) and w(j+1) are the real and imaginary parts of a complex eigenvalue, the corresponding complex eigenvector is computed if either `SELECT(j)` or `SELECT(j+1)` is .TRUE., and on exit `SELECT(j)` is set to .TRUE. and `SELECT(j+1)` is set to .FALSE.. Not referenced if `HOWMNY = 'A'` or 'B'.
- `N`: The order of the matrix T. $N \ge 0$.
- `T`: The upper quasi-triangular matrix T in Schur canonical form.
- `VL`: On entry, if `SIDE = 'L'` or 'B' and `HOWMNY = 'B'`, `VL` must contain an N-by-N matrix Q (usually the orthogonal matrix Q of Schur vectors returned by DHSEQR). On exit, if `SIDE = 'L'` or 'B', `VL` contains: if `HOWMNY = 'A'`, the matrix Y of left eigenvectors of T; if `HOWMNY = 'B'`, the matrix $Q \, Y$; if `HOWMNY = 'S'`, the left eigenvectors of T specified by

  -   `SELECT`, stored consecutively in the columns
  -   of `VL`, in the same order as their
  -   eigenvalues.

  A complex eigenvector corresponding to a complex eigenvalue is stored in two consecutive columns, the first holding the real part, and the second the imaginary part. Not referenced if `SIDE = 'R'`.
- `VR`: On entry, if `SIDE = 'R'` or 'B' and `HOWMNY = 'B'`, `VR` must contain an N-by-N matrix Q (usually the orthogonal matrix Q of Schur vectors returned by DHSEQR). On exit, if `SIDE = 'R'` or 'B', `VR` contains: if `HOWMNY = 'A'`, the matrix X of right eigenvectors of T; if `HOWMNY = 'B'`, the matrix $Q \, X$; if `HOWMNY = 'S'`, the right eigenvectors of T specified by

  -   `SELECT`, stored consecutively in the columns
  -   of `VR`, in the same order as their
  -   eigenvalues.

  A complex eigenvector corresponding to a complex eigenvalue is stored in two consecutive columns, the first holding the real part and the second the imaginary part. Not referenced if `SIDE = 'L'`.
- `mm`: The number of columns in the arrays `VL` and/or `VR`. $\mathrm{MM} \ge M$.
- `M`: The number of columns in the arrays `VL` and/or `VR` actually used to store the eigenvectors. If `HOWMNY = 'A'` or 'B', M is set to N. Each selected real eigenvector occupies one column and each selected complex eigenvector occupies two columns.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "both", "left", "right"
- `TypeError` third argument must be one of the following: "all", "backtransform", "selected"
- `RangeError` sixth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` eighth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )`
- `RangeError` tenth argument is invalid (column-major: rejected when `LDVL < 1 \|\| ( ( side === "left" \|\| side === "both" ) && LDVL < N )`)
- `RangeError` tenth argument is invalid (row-major: rejected when `LDVL < 1 \|\| ( ( side === "left" \|\| side === "both" ) && LDVL < max( 1, mm ) )`)
- `RangeError` twelfth argument is invalid (column-major: rejected when `LDVR < 1 \|\| ( ( side === "right" \|\| side === "both" ) && LDVR < N )`)
- `RangeError` twelfth argument is invalid (row-major: rejected when `LDVR < 1 \|\| ( ( side === "right" \|\| side === "both" ) && LDVR < max( 1, mm ) )`)
- `TypeError` if a string argument is not a valid option

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dtrevc3.ndarray(
    side, howmny,
    SELECT, strideSELECT, offsetSELECT,
    N,
    T, strideT1, strideT2, offsetT,
    VL, strideVL1, strideVL2, offsetVL,
    VR, strideVR1, strideVR2, offsetVR,
    mm,
    M,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork
) → integer
```

Computes some or all of the right and/or left eigenvectors of a real.
upper quasi-triangular matrix T.

The right eigenvector x and the left eigenvector y of T corresponding
to an eigenvalue w are defined by:
  T_x = w_x,     y**T _ T = w _ y**T

As in the reference, the back-transformation (`howmny = 'backtransform'`) is
blocked (NB vectors at a time, with dgemm) when WORK has room for it, and
done one vector at a time otherwise.

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `side` | `"left" \| "right" \| "both"` | `'right'`, `'left'`, or `'both'` |
| `howmny` | `"all" \| "backtransform" \| "selected"` | `'all'`, `'backtransform'`, or `'selected'` |
| `SELECT` | `Uint8Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Boolean selection array (used only if howmny=`'selected'`) |
| ↳ `strideSELECT` | `integer` | Stride for SELECT |
| ↳ `offsetSELECT` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Offset for SELECT |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of matrix T<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `T` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | Quasi-triangular Schur matrix (N x N) |
| ↳ `strideT1` | `integer` | First dimension stride of T |
| ↳ `strideT2` | `integer` | Second dimension stride of T |
| ↳ `offsetT` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Offset for T |
| `VL` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × mm</sub> | **in/out** · Left eigenvector matrix (N x MM) |
| ↳ `strideVL1` | `integer` | First dimension stride of VL |
| ↳ `strideVL2` | `integer` | Second dimension stride of VL |
| ↳ `offsetVL` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Offset for VL |
| `VR` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × mm</sub> | **in/out** · Right eigenvector matrix (N x MM) |
| ↳ `strideVR1` | `integer` | First dimension stride of VR |
| ↳ `strideVR2` | `integer` | Second dimension stride of VR |
| ↳ `offsetVR` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Offset for VR |
| `mm` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of columns available in VL/VR |
| `M` | `Int32Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the number of columns in the arrays VL and/or VR actually used to store the eigenvectors |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length ≥ max(1, 3 * N)</sub> | **out** · Workspace; length from `offsetWork` at least `max(1,3*N)`; when back-transforming, a length of at least `N + 2*N*8` enables the blocked back-transformation, and `N + 2*N*NB` (NB from `ilaenv`) is optimal |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | Stride for WORK (must be 1) |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Offset for WORK |

<details>

Not referenced if `HOWMNY = 'A'` or 'B'.

On exit, if `SIDE = 'R'` or 'B', `VR` contains: if `HOWMNY = 'A'`, the matrix X of right eigenvectors of T; if `HOWMNY = 'B'`, the matrix $Q \, X$; if `HOWMNY = 'S'`, the right eigenvectors of T specified by

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "both", "left", "right"
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "all", "backtransform", "selected"
- `RangeError` sixth argument must be a nonnegative integer

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N === 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import Int32Array from '@stdlib/array/int32/lib/index.js';
import Uint8Array from '@stdlib/array/uint8/lib/index.js';
import dtrevc3 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dtrevc3';

// Upper triangular matrix T in Schur canonical form (column-major):
const N = 3;
const T = new Float64Array( [ 1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 2.0, 3.0, 0.0, 4.0, 5.0, 6.0 ] );
const SELECT = new Uint8Array( N );
const M = new Int32Array( 1 );
const WORK = new Float64Array( 3 * N );

// Using the standard interface (compute all right eigenvectors):
let VL = new Float64Array( N * N );
let VR = new Float64Array( N * N );
let info = dtrevc3( 'column-major', 'right', 'all', SELECT, 1, N, T, N, VL, N, VR, N, N, M, WORK );
console.log( info, M[ 0 ], VR );

// Using the ndarray interface:
VL = new Float64Array( N * N );
VR = new Float64Array( N * N );
info = dtrevc3.ndarray( 'right', 'all', SELECT, 1, 0, N, T, 1, N, 0, VL, 1, N, 0, VR, 1, N, 0, N, M, WORK, 1, 0 );
console.log( info, M[ 0 ], VR );
```

</section>

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DTREVC3`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DTREVC3 computes some or all of the right and/or left eigenvectors of a real upper quasi-triangular matrix T. Matrices of this type are produced by the Schur factorization of a real general matrix: $A = Q \, T \, Q^T$, as computed by DHSEQR.

The right eigenvector x and the left eigenvector y of T corresponding to an eigenvalue w are defined by:

$$
T \, x = w \, x, (y^T) \, T = w \, (y^T)
$$

where $y^T$ denotes the transpose of the vector y. The eigenvalues are not input to this routine, but are read directly from the diagonal blocks of T.

This routine returns the matrices X and/or Y of right and left eigenvectors of T, or the products $Q \, X$ and/or $Q \, Y$, where Q is an input matrix. If Q is the orthogonal factor that reduces a matrix A to Schur form T, then $Q \, X$ and $Q \, Y$ are the matrices of right and left eigenvectors of A.

This uses a Level 3 BLAS version of the back transformation.

### Further Details

The algorithm used in this program is basically backward (forward) substitution, with scaling to make the the code robust against possible overflow.

Each eigenvector is normalized so that the element of largest magnitude has magnitude 1; here the magnitude of a complex number (x,y) is taken to be \|x\| + \|y\|.

</section>
